_purpose: Two Blueprints where one inherits from the other and calls a function it declares. Editing the base and recompiling must leave the child compiling clean; taking that function away must leave the child REPORTED broken rather than quietly stale. The second half is the one worth having - a compile result that only ever says 'compiled' is not a compile result, and a dependent that reads fine while its parent no longer offers what it calls is the bug an agent cannot see.
_note: Deletion order matters both ways round: the child holds a reference to the base, so it goes first at both ends of the file.

steps._note: Housekeeping: clear debris from an aborted earlier run, child before base.
The thing the child will depend on. It has to exist and be compiled before the child is created, or the child's skeleton never inherits it.
Parented off the class the previous create returned, rather than a path retyped by hand.
The dependency, made real: BeginPlay into a call of the inherited function. class 'self' resolves against this blueprint's own skeleton, which is where an inherited function lives.
A change to the base that does not touch what the child uses.
The child still compiles - recompiling a base does not invalidate a dependent that was not relying on anything that moved.
Now take the function away. The base itself is fine - nothing in it referred to the function - so this step succeeds.

And the child is reported broken. bp_compile fails on a blueprint with errors rather than returning a clean report with an error count buried in it, which is why this is expect_failure rather than an expect of errors:1.

The blueprint is left broken on purpose and then deleted. Restoring the function and recompiling would be a second claim - whether a dangling call heals when its target comes back - and it is not the one this file is making.
